relationship.original_equation: Company sales = industry sales × company market share
relationship.locator: Converting Industry Forecast to Company Sales Forecast

assumptions: Company and industry sales refer to the same market boundary, accounting basis, currency and period.

limitations: This identity does not establish future sales or recommend an investment.
Revenue share and unit-volume share are not interchangeable when prices differ.

models.title: Noncash working capital proportional to sales
models.summary: The simplified example sets noncash working capital at a fixed fraction of annual sales.

relationship.original_equation: Noncash working capital = sales × noncash working capital fraction
relationship.locator: Unit 12, section 12.7, percent of sales approach, printed pp185–186
relationship.translation_notes: The fraction is a dimensionless ratio of a balance to period sales; working capital can be negative.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Noncash working capital balance expressed relative to sales for the same period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Noncash working capital and sales refer to the same business, currency and explicitly matched balance date and sales period.
The supplied fraction is appropriate for the intended working-capital definition and excludes cash.
limitations: The public source gives a general working-capital relation; the owner example specifies noncash working capital.
A constant fraction is a modeling assumption, not an independently validated prediction.
This is a balance; investment in working capital is the change between balances.
